newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-HOPES HIGH FOR NATIONAL WINNER.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-HOPES HIGH FOR NATIONAL WINNER.

text.p: Grand National winner Rough Quest is set to run in Kempton's King George VI Chase on Thursday but because of the fast ground a final decision will not be made until the morning of the race.
Rough Quest's trainer Terry Casey decided on Tuesday the horse could take his chance in the jumping season's mid-winter highlight if conditions did not worsen.
He said: "At the moment we are running. It's fast and it's not ideal but it is raceable."
Rough Quest is a National winner with a touch of class and he will need it to shake up last year's King George winner and the hot 4-6 favourite One Man.
"One Man is a very good horse but I hope Rough Quest will run very well. Some people say he doesn't like going right-handed but don't forget he won the Racing Post Chase at Kempton.
If he runs, Rough Quest will probably start at around 7-2 with the next in the betting at about 10-1.
Without the Aintree winner, One Man, a striking grey horse, trained by Gordon Richards and ridden by Richard Dunwoody, should have an easy task.
His only failure last season was in the Cheltenham Gold Cup but he looked to have put that behind him with an easy win recently at Wetherby.

Mr Mulligan, trained by Noel Chance, may prove best of the others, after recovering from a foot injury. Barton Bank, to be ridden by Adrian Maguire, appears held on the form book, but has a good record in the race, including winning it in 1993.
Strong Promise will like the ground and has had a good season but he is still in the novice stage.
Should overnight frost or snow intervene and prevent the race being run on Thursday or Friday, it will be re-scheduled for Sandown on Saturday week.
Betting: 4-6 One Man, 7-2 Rough Quest, 10-1 Mr Mulligan, 12-1 Barton Bank, 14-1 Strong Promise 16-1 and upwards others.
